cover.title: Director
cover.tagline: The AI agent team that lets a single founder run a $5M nonprofit with no back-office staff
cover.subtagline: Turning under-resourced founders into fundable, operationally tight organizations
cover.oneliner: Short term, we're a forward-deployed AI support team. Long term, we're building the autopilot that runs the entire nonprofit back office so a single founder can run a $5M org with almost no internal ops staff.

slides.title: Problem – Founders Are the Whole Leadership Team
slides.subtitle: Nonprofit founders are carrying 5 jobs on 1 salary.
slides.highlight: Promising orgs plateau at $300–600k or quietly shut down — not for lack of impact, but for lack of backbone.
slides.footnote: When funding tightens and staff are cut, all of this collapses back onto one person. Right now, most of their time and money are trapped in back-office work that should be automated.

image.placeholder: Photorealistic image of overwhelmed nonprofit founder, stressed out, managing 5 different jobs, looking at one phone while talking on a second phone, laptop open with multiple browser tabs, sticky notes everywhere, in a small cluttered office

slides.title: Ideal Customer – Downshifted Orgs (Beachhead)
slides.subtitle: Our initial focus: orgs that already proved they can raise $400k–$1M.

sections.heading: These orgs:
items: Have real donor and community relationships
Have a history of 7-figure budgets or close

sections.heading: But in the current funding environment:
items: The founder is back to doing everything
Many are considering shutting down despite strong demand

slides.highlight: These leaders don't need another tool. They need a backbone.
slides.footnote: This hits founders of color especially hard, as equity-era funding retrenches.

image.placeholder: Photorealistic image of a nonprofit leader alone in a half-empty office, packing boxes, looking exhausted but determined, wall behind shows framed photos of community events and a chart with a line that rose then fell

slides.title: Ideal Customer – Foundations as Buyers
slides.subtitle: Foundations can sponsor multiple orgs at once.

sections.heading: The opportunity:
items: Foundations already fund capacity-building for grantees
They can purchase Director packages for 5–10 orgs

sections.heading: Why this works:
items: Foundations get measurable capacity ROI across portfolio
Orgs get backbone support they couldn't afford alone

slides.highlight: A single foundation can unlock Director for an entire cohort of grantees.

image.placeholder: Photorealistic image of a foundation program officer in a modern glass office building meeting room, laptop showing a portfolio dashboard, shaking hands with multiple nonprofit leaders visible through glass walls, conveying partnership and scale

slides.title: Market Opportunity
slides.subtitle: A massive, underserved market ready for AI-native solutions.

sections.heading: TAM: $164B – Total US Nonprofit Administrative Spending
items: Nonprofit sector contributes $1.4 trillion to GDP
This spending is ripe for AI automation

sections.heading: SAM: $3.5B – Small/Mid Nonprofits ($250k–$2M budgets)
items: Existing solutions: $5.5B nonprofit software + $6.7B consulting market

slides.highlight: 68% of nonprofits now use AI (up from 58% in 2023). The market is ready for an AI-native backbone.
slides.footnote: Sources: Independent Sector, Statista, NCCS, Google for Nonprofits Survey 2025, Intent Market Research

image.placeholder: Clean infographic with three concentric circles showing market size: outer ring labeled TAM $164B (all US nonprofit admin spending), middle ring SAM $3.5B (small/mid nonprofits), inner circle SOM $50M (5-year target), with icons representing nonprofits at different scales

slides.title: Broken Options
slides.subtitle: Existing solutions don't fit this stage.

sections.heading: DIY SaaS stack
sections.text: CRMs, grant tools, accounting, email… Founders don't have time to integrate and maintain them.

sections.heading: Consultants & agencies
sections.text: Project-based, expensive, seen as "overhead." Advice without ongoing responsibility.

slides.highlight: There is no integrated, AI-native backbone designed for $400k–$1M orgs that have real relationships but no team.
slides.footnote: $360–450k/year for the backbone on a fragile budget.

slides.title: The Director Pod – Capacity Ramp
slides.subtitle: Pods scale from 4 → 8 → 16 orgs as the OS and agents mature.

sections.heading: Phase 2 – 8 orgs
sections.text: Mature core agents handle repetitive tasks. Same structure supports more orgs.

sections.heading: Phase 3 – 16 orgs
sections.text: 2+ FDDs. Standardized playbooks. Agents do recurring work.

sections.heading: Phase 4 – 100+ orgs
items: AI-native director team handles 90–95% of recurring work
Pod becomes supervisory layer, not execution layer
Single founder safely runs $3–5M org with no internal back-office hires

slides.subtitle: From forward-deployed support team to fully autonomous nonprofit autopilot.

items: AI agents assist with finance, ops, comms, and donor prep

sections.heading: Future (Where We're Going)
items: Fully AI-native director team for finance, ops, comms, development
Agents handle 90–95% of recurring back-office work
Founders and boards focus almost entirely on programs and relationships

slides.highlight: Audacious goal: No nonprofit ever dies because of operations, fundraising, or compliance again — only because the mission is done.

slides.title: Economics – Why This Makes Sense
slides.subtitle: Director makes a serious backbone affordable and scalable.

sections.heading: With Director:
items: Long term, as a Pod supervises 100+ orgs, backbone costs can drop by ~80%, shifting dollars from administration back into programs

slides.footnote: As Pods scale, pod-level gross margins expand while keeping human leadership involvement high.

image.placeholder: Clean bar chart comparing costs: tall red bar labeled 'Traditional Backbone $360-450k/year' with icons for ED, Ops, Dev, Comms roles, versus shorter green bar labeled 'With Director $180-270k/year' showing ED + Director Pod, with '$100-180k SAVED' callout and arrow

slides.title: Why Now – AI Agents + Nonprofit Pressure
slides.subtitle: Two timing curves are intersecting.

sections.heading: Agentic AI is production-ready:
items: "AI coworkers" already shipping in engineering, finance, and customer ops
Small human teams can manage far more complexity with agents

sections.heading: Nonprofits are under structural pressure:
items: Orgs with $1M+ budgets are losing staff
Funders want grantees with credible backbones and visibility

sections.heading: The opportunity:
items: For the first time, it's realistic to imagine automating 90–95% of nonprofit back-office work and letting a single founder safely run a $3–5M org with almost no internal ops staff

slides.highlight: Director sits at this intersection: an AI-native backbone delivered by a lean, forward-deployed team to orgs that cannot justify rebuilding full in-house leadership.

image.placeholder: Elegant chart showing two rising trend lines intersecting at 'NOW': blue line labeled 'AI Agent Capability' rising steeply from 2020-2025, red line labeled 'Nonprofit Operational Pressure' also rising, intersection point highlighted with 'Director' logo at the sweet spot

slides.title: Strategic Partners & Structure
slides.subtitle: HiiiWAV is our 501(c)(3) partner for philanthropic capacity-building.

sections.heading: HiiiWAV (501c3)
items: Founded by Bosko Kante, focused on arts and social impact
Serves as philanthropic conduit for capacity-building grants to orgs Director serves
Enables foundations and donors to fund nonprofit backbone capacity tax-deductibly

sections.heading: How it works:
items: Foundations grant to HiiiWAV for capacity-building programs
HiiiWAV funds nonprofits' access to Director services
Director provides backbone support; philanthropic dollars stay with nonprofits

sections.heading: Governance & Conflict Management:
items: Independent HiiiWAV board approves all Director-related arrangements
Bosko recuses from any HiiiWAV decisions involving Director
Arms-length pricing; written conflict of interest policy on file

slides.highlight: This structure lets philanthropic dollars flow to under-resourced nonprofits while Director operates as a sustainable, investor-backed business.

image.placeholder: Clean flow diagram showing structure: Foundation icons at top flowing dollars down to HiiiWAV 501(c)(3) in center, which grants to Nonprofit org icons below, while Director (shown as service arrows) provides backbone support to the same nonprofits - illustrating philanthropic and service flows
